```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(GPTLasso)
library(MultiAssayExperiment)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
```

# Overview

GPTLasso combines multiview cooperative learning with multistudy
pretraining. Public interfaces accept either the PCL-style list or a
`MultiAssayExperiment` (MAE). A PCL contains a feature-by-sample
`feature_table`, `sample_metadata` with `sample_id`, `study`, and `Y`,
and `feature_metadata` with `featureID` plus a view column. MAE
experiments represent views, `colData()` stores `study` and `Y`, and
`sampleMap()` connects assay columns to primary samples. Training and
prediction containers may use different supported formats when their
layouts match.

# Simulated PCL input

The simulation wrappers return ready-to-fit PCL objects.

```{r pcl-input}
simulated <- sim.gaussian.data(nsample = c(15, 15), nstudy = 2,
                               de.prob = rep(0.5, 3), seed = 101)
pcl_train <- simulated$x_train
names(pcl_train)
dim(pcl_train$feature_table)
table(pcl_train$sample_metadata$study)
table(pcl_train$feature_metadata$featureType)
```

# Alternative MAE input

Assay column identifiers may differ from primary sample identifiers
because the mapping, rather than name equality, controls alignment.

```{r constructor}
make_example <- function(n_study = 2L, n_view = 2L, family = "gaussian") {
    set.seed(101)
    n_each <- 12L
    n <- n_study * n_each
    primary <- paste0("sample", seq_len(n))
    study <- rep(paste0("study", seq_len(n_study)), each = n_each)
    experiments <- lapply(seq_len(n_view), function(view) {
        mat <- matrix(rnorm(4 * n), nrow = 4)
        rownames(mat) <- paste0("feature", seq_len(4))
        colnames(mat) <- paste0("view", view, "_column", seq_len(n))
        SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(value = mat))
    })
    names(experiments) <- paste0("view", seq_len(n_view))
    signal <- colSums(assay(experiments[[1]])[1:2, , drop = FALSE])
    Y <- switch(family,
        gaussian = signal + rnorm(n),
        binomial = rbinom(n, 1, plogis(scale(signal))),
        cox = I(survival::Surv(rexp(n, exp(scale(signal))),
                               rep(c(0, 1), length.out = n)))
    )
    map <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(experiments), function(view) {
        S4Vectors::DataFrame(
            assay = factor(view, levels = names(experiments)),
            primary = primary, colname = colnames(experiments[[view]]))
    }))
    MultiAssayExperiment(
        experiments = ExperimentList(experiments),
        colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(study = study, Y = Y,
                                       row.names = primary),
        sampleMap = map
    )
}

mae <- make_example()
mae
sampleMap(mae)
```

For partial overlap, preprocess explicitly with `intersectColumns()`.
GPTLasso requires every selected view to map exactly once to every
primary sample.

# Four supported layouts

```{r layouts}
multi_study_multi_view <- make_example(2, 2)
multi_study_one_view <- make_example(2, 1)
one_study_multi_view <- make_example(1, 2)
one_study_one_view <- make_example(1, 1)
c(MSMV = length(experiments(multi_study_multi_view)),
  MSOV = length(experiments(multi_study_one_view)),
  OSMV = length(experiments(one_study_multi_view)),
  OSOV = length(experiments(one_study_one_view)))
```

With one view, effective rho is 0; transfer alpha remains meaningful
across studies. With one study, effective alpha is 1; rho remains
tunable across views. All cases return the same GPTLasso classes.

# Complete Gaussian workflow

```{r gaussian-fit}
fit <- gptLasso(pcl_train, alpha.ptlasso = 0.5,
                rho = c(0, 1), family = "gaussian",
                type.measure = "mse", nfolds = 3)
class(fit)
fit[c("alpha.ptlasso", "fitoverall.rho", "target.study.names")]

prediction <- predict(fit, simulated$x_test, type = "response")
names(prediction$yhatpre)
prediction$metrics$MSE
```

`target` restricts individual and pretrained fits while the overall
stage still uses all studies. `fitoverall`, `fitind`, and `fitpre`
expose the three stages; `support.vars` contains the overall all-study
model support.

# Reduced layouts

```{r reduced-fits}
one_view_fit <- gptLasso(multi_study_one_view, alpha.ptlasso = 0.5,
                         rho = c(0, 1), nfolds = 3)
c(effective = one_view_fit$rho, requested = one_view_fit$rho.requested)

one_study_fit <- gptLasso(one_study_multi_view, alpha.ptlasso = 0.25,
                          rho = c(0, 1), nfolds = 3)
c(effective = one_study_fit$alpha.ptlasso,
  requested = one_study_fit$alpha.ptlasso.requested)
```

# Cross-validation and assay selection

For MAE input, `assay.names = NULL` requires one assay per experiment. A
scalar selects the same name everywhere; a named vector selects one
assay per experiment. `assay.names` must be `NULL` for PCL input.

```{r cross-validation}
cvfit <- cv.gptLasso(pcl_train,
                     alpha.ptlasso.list = c(0, 0.5, 1),
                     rho = c(0, 1), nfolds = 3)
cvfit$alpha.ptlasso.hat
cvfit$errpre
```

# Binomial and Cox outcomes

Use `family = "binomial"` with AUC or deviance. Cox outcomes must be
`Surv` objects; event-stratified folds support deviance or concordance
(`"C"`).

```{r other-families, eval=FALSE}
binary_mae <- make_example(2, 2, family = "binomial")
binary_fit <- gptLasso(binary_mae, family = "binomial",
                       type.measure = "auc", rho = c(0, 1), nfolds = 3)

cox_mae <- make_example(2, 2, family = "cox")
cox_fit <- gptLasso(cox_mae, family = "cox", type.measure = "C",
                    rho = c(0, 1), nfolds = 3)
predict(cox_fit, cox_mae, type = "link")
```

# Installation and references

Install through Bioconductor with `BiocManager::install("GPTLasso")`.
GPTLasso builds on `glmnet`, `multiview`, and Bioconductor's MAE
infrastructure.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
